interest: Shows 1947 peace-treaty talks on protecting migratory birds like the Emperor Goose crossing Japan and Alaska.
overview: Gabrielson and Flory discuss adding Japan peace-treaty protections for migratory birds like the Emperor Goose, which breeds in Alaska and winters in Japan, plus Bering Sea pelagic seabirds.

people.name: William E. S. Flory
people.role: Official, International Resources Division, Department of State

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum recording a conversation with Ira N. Gabrielson concerning migratory bird protection provisions in the proposed Japanese Peace Treaty.
subfiles.from: William E. S. Flory (International Resources Division, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Flory records Gabrielson urging Japan treaty protection for migratory birds like the Emperor Goose and various pelagic seabirds.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Wildlife Protection in the Japanese Treaty

subfiles.about: A letter from Ira N. Gabrielson advising the State Department on the extent to which pelagic and migratory birds require treaty protection in Japanese waters and the Bering Sea.
subfiles.from: Ira N. Gabrielson (President, Wildlife Management Institute)
subfiles.summary: Gabrielson names the Emperor Goose as the main bird crossing Japan and Alaska, suggesting pelagic-bird protections too.
subfiles.title: Letter from Ira N. Gabrielson to William E. S. Flory regarding Pelagic and Migratory Bird Protection
subfiles.to: William E. S. Flory (International Resources Division, Department of State)
